title: indigo_mount_synscan: a lost UDP reply costs a full 1 s command timeout and lengthens guide pulses
description:
Found on 2026-11-21 on the AZ-GTi (firmware 3.16, UDP over Wi-Fi) by the recorded hardware run of ticket 6a4e8bdf-ff81-4031-8723-df3f84d73b8a: synscan_guide_pulse_accuracy failed in two recorded runs and once alone (RA pulses +816.8 ms, +1148.8 ms, +1242.4 ms too long; limit 400 ms). The driver debug log shows 'No SynScan response before timeout' for a poll command (:j2) and for a pulse command (:I); each lost reply costs the 1 s SYNSCAN_COMMAND_TIMEOUT before the retry, so the end of a guide pulse is delayed by about 1 s, and if the reply to the command ending the pulse is lost the mount physically guides about 1 s longer. A read-only probe of 400 queries lost 2 replies (0.5 %); replies took 9.6 ms median, 19.2 ms maximum. On 2026-11-19 the same case passed 21/21.

To do: decide and implement how the driver retries a UDP command whose reply is lost (shorter per-attempt timeout for UDP, number of attempts, whether serial keeps the present timing; consider commands that are not idempotent and a reply that arrives late and could be taken for the next command's reply), keep guide pulse timing independent of a lost poll reply where possible, model reply loss in the simulator (drop every Nth reply or a named command) and add simulator cases that fail before the change. Bump the driver version. Recorded simulator run and a non-interactive hardware run on the AZ-GTi (no hot-plug). Ticket 6a4e8bdf stays open until a clean recorded hardware run; its harness change is reviewed and independent of this defect.

outcome.summary: BLOCKING (regression in kind from the 0.2 s UDP timeout, reproduced): a late reply to an earlier attempt of a retried query is taken as the reply to the NEXT query of the same reply length. synscan_reply_length() only rejects datagrams of a different length (.driver:283-293, :364-380), and the zero-wait drain (:421-428) only removes datagrams that have already arrived. Once a reply is slower than 0.2 s, the command is resent and completes on whichever reply comes first; the other reply arrives during a later command's wait. For :j2/:j1 (both 6 digits) that puts the DEC counter into the RA slot, and for :f1/:f2 (both 3) the status of the wrong axis is used. The GoTo and park finalizers read :f1 then :f2, so they can end a slew while one axis still runs, and the DEC pulse stop polling can misread the axis state. Under sustained 0.2-0.4 s latency (the AZ-GTi measurements in this ticket show a 5 s episode of 250-420 ms replies) the shift cascades through every same-length query of a burst. Reproduced in a scratch copy (own Makefile.inc, scratch dylibs) with a probe on the UDP simulator: GoTo to DEC 20, after a poll the faults ':j2 late:250 1' and ':j1 late:100 1' (a measured slow reply followed by a routine 100 ms spike). With the ticket driver, the raw RA published by the next poll jumped 10.31 h (the DEC counter as RA), i.e. another axis's value on the bus. With the master driver (1 s timeout, no resend) all 3 rounds deviated at most 0.001 h. This breaks the owner's rule that the driver never publishes another frame's values, even transiently, and it is the late-reply case the ticket asked to consider. Re-review of 1b0415204 (delta from 0cb794c48). Stray-reply finding: fixed for positions and status. My probe (GoTo DEC 20, ':j2 late:250 1' + ':j1 late:100 1') and three consecutive retried-query variants not covered by a case (':j2 late:250 1/:j1 late:250 1', ':j2 late:350 1/:j1 late:100 1', ':j2 late:450 2/:j1 late:150 1') all keep RA within 0.0014 h; on 0cb794c48 the first variant still jumps 10.32 h. The new cases late_dec_reply_is_not_taken_for_ra, late_status_reply_does_not_end_goto and sustained_latency_keeps_positions pass. BLOCKING (regression introduced by the new stray wait; it contradicts the ticket's pulse-timing goal and the note's own claim that the end of a pulse is not held): synscan_slew_axis_at_rate() (indigo_mount_synscan.driver:738) sends the status query :f1 before the :I1 period change both at the start and at the end of an RA pulse. When the start :f1 is retried, a stray of length 3 is recorded until last send + 0.5 s, and synscan_drain_udp() (driver ~:425-441) makes the end-of-pulse :f1, a query of the same length, wait for it before the :I1 that restores tracking. If the lost datagram never arrives (a lost request or a lost reply), the RA pulse physically runs until that deadline. Reproduced in a scratch copy with the ':f1 lost 1' fault armed before an RA pulse on the UDP guiding fixture: 100 ms pulse physical +407 ms / completion +610 ms, 300 ms pulse +201 / +413 ms. With the 0cb794c48 driver the same probe gives +5 / +207 and +11 / +223. So one lost datagram now lengthens a short guide pulse by up to 0.4 s, and completion +610 ms would fail the 400 ms hardware limit. Suggested fix: record the command with each stray and make a query wait only for strays of a different command with the same reply length (:j1 vs :j2, :f1 vs :f2). A stray of the same command is that command's answer, exactly as the design already accepts within its own retries, so the end-of-pulse :f1 (and a repeated poll query) would not wait. Then add a case: RA pulse of 1

Third round, d2bcae094 (delta from 1b0415204). My blocking pulse finding is fixed. In a scratch copy (own Makefile.inc and dylibs, under the lock), with ':f1 lost 1' armed before an RA pulse on the UDP guiding fixture: 100 ms pulse physical +10 / completion +216 ms, 300 ms pulse +4 / +214 ms; on 1b0415204 it was +407/+610 and +201/+413. Position and status mix-ups still do not occur: my three retried-query variants keep RA within 0.0014 h. Accounting (driver:370-560: synscan_add_stray, synscan_take_stray :407, synscan_foreign_stray_deadline, synscan_drain_udp :443, synscan_command :518). Every UDP send is recorded when written. A reply or '!' on attempt k is credited to the oldest send of the same command, so k-1 sends stay outstanding; total failure leaves all k. When a same-command stray is taken as the answer, the latest send stays recorded, so the count cannot drift. Entries expire at send + 0.5 s; with 16 entries the oldest is dropped; stray_count is reset on close (:1631). Because a query waits for strays of other commands with the same reply length before it sends, at most one query command per reply length can have outstanding sends at any time (expiry excepted). So crediting an other-length datagram to the oldest send of that length always hits the right command, and errors in crediting only cause an unnecessary bounded wait, never a missed one. Late '!' and garbled datagrams are not credited, so the entry they answered only causes such a bounded wait. The worst wait is about 0.5 s once per command (strays are added only as sends happen), so a UDP command takes at most about 1.1 s on the queue, abort and disconnect included. Same-command stale reply (question 3), NON-BLOCKING: I tried to provoke a GoTo finalizer ending early with a stale RA status left over from the handler's stop wait (':f1 late:450 1 / late:0 1 / late:150 1', 3 rounds). It does not happen: the DEC stop wait's :f2 waits for the foreign :f1 stray (0.25 s seen in the simulator command log) a

Round 4, 4df2b94b2 (delta from d2bcae094, including merge 0a0e43fd6). Hardware diagnosis confirmed from 4e2005ec_r4_diag1.log: the :j2 sent at 12:37:41.120 got no reply, the repeat (41.331) was answered at 41.345, and :j1 went out only at 41.838, after the 0.5 s foreign-stray wait; the poll held the queue 0.766 s. My round-3 pass accepted that fallback cost as bounded; on hardware it is what broke the pulse case. The order log shows 905 of 905 complete pairs in order. The recorded run 4e2005ec_r4_hw_run.log is 21/21 with the pulse table as noted. ORDER MARKER (synscan_resync_udp, driver:471, called at :606 after a UDP command that needed more than one send): it reads until the 2-digit :g1 reply and then forgets every outstanding send, which is exact if replies keep their order; otherwise the per-send deadlines remain. Paths probed in a scratch copy on a retried :j2 (late 250 ms or lost): marker lost, marker 300 ms late, marker refused ('!0'), marker answered with 6 digits, :j2 lost plus marker lost, :j2 450 ms late plus marker 100 ms late. All 6 keep RA/DEC at the mount's position (max 0.0014 h), publish no coordinate ALERT and leave no pending fault. The RA query follows the repeated DEC query 257-368 ms later when the marker cannot help and 502-507 ms later in the fallback cases; the worst case per command is bounded at about 0.6 s plus the marker's 0.2 s plus at most one 0.5 s foreign wait. A late marker reply is credited to the :g1 send; a later :g1 query treats it as its own answer, which is the same value, and :g2 waits for it as a foreign stray. No marker is sent while one is outstanding. The marker write does not touch last_send_time, the serial path is untouched, close resets the strays, and configure needs no reset. Controllers that cannot answer :g1 with two hex digits cannot connect, because configure requires :g1/:g2 (driver ~:1507), so a different length or an error reply can only be transient and then falls back to the deadlines without harm (probed).

1. Current transaction (indigo_mount_synscan.driver, version 26)
- synscan_command(): before every attempt indigo_uni_discard() (on UDP a 10 ms select per call, visible as "// timeout" before each command in guide_debug.log, so every UDP command costs ~10 ms extra), write "<cmd>\r", synscan_read_response(). Serial: 1 attempt, indigo_uni_read_section2() with 1 s first-byte / 0.1 s next-byte timeout. UDP: SYNSCAN_UDP_COMMAND_ATTEMPTS = 3, each indigo_uni_wait_for_data(SYNSCAN_COMMAND_TIMEOUT = 1 s) + one datagram read; a '!' reply ends the command at once, a missing/garbled one is retried. Worst UDP transaction 3.03 s.
- Late replies: the discard before each attempt drains datagrams that already arrived (one 1-byte read per datagram drops the whole datagram on Linux/macOS). A reply arriving after that discard but before the next reply is taken as the next command's reply. Queries are shape-checked only by callers (synscan_valid_payload, payload length 6/3/2); setting commands accept any "=...\r", so a late "=XXXXXX" would be taken as an :I/:J acknowledgement. One misattribution then self-heals (the displaced reply is drained by the following discard).
- Windows (source audit, not reproduced): read_data() uses recv() with the caller's length; indigo_uni_discard() reads 1 byte, so a pending datagram gives WSAEMSGSIZE, which latches handle->last_error and silently kills the UDP session (synscan_validate_handle() never reports UDP loss). Any late reply on Windows is therefore fatal today.
- Non-idempotent resends: queries, :E :F :G :I :K :L :M :O :P :V and the :W encoder/PPEC on/off settings are idempotent. Risky: :J after :H (H is a relative increment; a resent :J after a short GOTO already finished could repeat the move if the firmware keeps the increment; the simulator clears it, real beh

Change (indigo_mount_synscan.driver, regenerated with the generator built in the worktree; .c diff mirrors the .driver diff):
- version 32 (:27); defines SYNSCAN_UDP_REPLY_TIMEOUT 0.2 s, SYNSCAN_POLL_GUIDE_GUARD 0.2, SYNSCAN_POLL_AFTER_GUIDE 0.05, SYNSCAN_POLL_GUIDE_STALE 2.0 (:48-53). SYNSCAN_UDP_COMMAND_ATTEMPTS 3 and serial timing (1 s / 0.1 s, one attempt, indigo_uni_discard) unchanged.
- synscan_now() uses indigo_monotonic_time() (:279); also used by motion_deadline. synscan_reply_length() (:283-293): 3 for :f, 2 for :g, 6 for other lowercase queries and :D, 0 for settings.
- synscan_read_response() takes the command (:355); on UDP waits until a 0.2 s attempt deadline and skips a '='-framed datagram whose payload length does not fit the command (:364-380); a right-length late reply is taken as the answer to the repeated command. '!' replies are not length-checked (an error reply cannot be attributed).
- synscan_command(): on UDP drains pending datagrams whole with indigo_uni_wait_for_data(handle, 0) + indigo_uni_read() instead of indigo_uni_discard() (:421-428); serial path unchanged.
- mount on_timer (:1935-1952): when a guide deadline is less than 0.2 s ahead (or passed by less than 2 s) the poll is rescheduled 50 ms after the deadline. The 2 s staleness bound is needed because a guider disconnect cancels the finalizer and leaves the deadline set (the generated guider connection handler calls indigo_cancel_pending_handlers()).
- No library or generator change.

Phase 1 analysis (no driver change in the worktree; prototype in a scratch copy only). Evidence: scratchpad/udp_4e20 (probe.py, run1.json, analyze.py, prototype_*.diff, proto_*.log).

1. Current transaction (indigo_mount_synscan.driver, version 26)
- synscan_command(): before every attempt indigo_uni_discard() (on UDP a 10 ms select per call, visible as "// timeout" before each command in guide_debug.log, so every UDP command costs ~10 ms extra), write "<cmd>\r", synscan_read_response(). Serial: 1 attempt, indigo_uni_read_section2() with 1 s first-byte / 0.1 s next-byte timeout. UDP: SYNSCAN_UDP_COMMAND_ATTEMPTS = 3, each indigo_uni_wait_for_data(SYNSCAN_COMMAND_TIMEOUT = 1 s) + one datagram read; a '!' reply ends the command at once, a missing/garbled one is retried. Worst UDP transaction 3.03 s.
- Late replies: the discard before each attempt drains datagrams that already arrived (one 1-byte read per datagram drops the whole datagram on Linux/macOS). A reply arriving after that discard but before the next reply is taken as the next command's reply. Queries are shape-checked only by callers (synscan_valid_payload, payload length 6/3/2); setting commands accept any "=...\r", so a late "=XXXXXX" would be taken as an :I/:J acknowledgement. One misattribution then self-heals (the displaced reply is drained by the following discard).
- Windows (source audit, not reproduced): read_data() uses recv() with the caller's length; indigo_uni_discard() reads 1 byte, so a pending datagram gives WSAEMSGSIZE, which latches handle->last_error and silently kills the UDP session (synscan_validate_handle() never reports UDP loss). Any late reply on Windows is therefore fatal today.
- Non-idempotent resends: queries, :E :F :G :I :K :L :M :O :P :V and the :W encoder/PPEC on/off settings are idempotent. Risky: :J after :H (H is a relative increment; a resent :J after a short GOTO already finished could repeat the move if the firmware keeps the increment; the simulator clears it, real behaviour unverified), :J on a running axis (if the firmware answers '!' the DEC pulse start fails with the axis left running and no finalizer), :W start-PPEC-training (may answer !7 when already started). All exist today with 3 attempts; a shorter timeout does not add resends after real losses, only after replies slower than the timeout.

2. Guide pulse timing
- RA (tracking, low speed): start = :f1 + :I1<guide period>, end = :f1 + :I1<tracking period>; no stop. DEC: start = :f2 [+ :G2 :I2] + :J2, end = :K2 + :f2 polling (100 ms sleeps). Deadline = synscan_now() (gettimeofday, wall clock) + duration, set before the start commands; the URGENT finalizer is scheduled `duration` after the start handler returns and rechecks the deadline. Handlers of mount, guider and aux share the master queue; the mount poll (on_timer, every 1 s idle / 0.5 s busy) reads :j2 :j1 (+ :d2 :d1 for X_ENCODER_POSITION) and cannot be preempted.
- Physical effect of one lost datagram (T = per-attempt timeout, today 1 s): start :f1 lost or start :I1 request lost -> pulse starts late, length correct, completion late by T; start :I1 reply lost (executed) -> physical +T (finalizer timed from handler end); end :f1 lost or end :I1 request lost -> physical +T; end :I1 reply lost -> length correct, completion late T; poll reply lost while the deadline passes -> finalizer waits for the poll, physical + up to T. Hardware log guide_debug.log shows exactly these: :j2 poll loss at 10:03:21.66 just as a pulse came due (finalizer ran at 22.785, +1.12 s) and :I15FC306 start-reply loss at 10:03:25.88 (+1.03 s).
- Even without loss the poll (4 x ~25 ms on hardware) delays a finalizer that comes due during it by up to ~100 ms.
- Pulse timing can be made largely independent of retry timing: (a) monotonic deadlines, (b) do not start a poll within a guard before a guide deadline (reschedule it after the deadline), (c) T bounds the remaining cases. A truly preemptive stop is not possible: the protocol has no timed pulse and replies are not tagged, so a stop cannot be interleaved with a transaction in flight.

3. AZ-GTi measurement (read-only :j1/:j2/:f1/:f2 by unicast to 192.168.111.139:11880, firmware reply =0310A5; broadcast skipped because a concurrent simulator test listened on loopback 11880; 3215 queries, 516 s, 3 s late-reply window after each loss)
- Overall: 26 lost (0.81 %), median 9.6 ms, p95 80 ms, p99 96 ms, max 419 ms. No stray or mismatched replies; exactly one late reply, 1580 ms after its :j1.
- Loss depends on idle time before the datagram: back-to-back 15 ms gaps 3/2000 (0.15 %); 100 ms gaps 5/600 (0.83 %); driver poll pattern (burst of 4 after 1 s idle) 12/600 (2.0 %), 8 of them on the first query of the burst = 5.3 % of polls; first query after 8 s idle 6/15 (40 %). Consistent with Wi-Fi power save (mount MAC is Espressif, 5c:cf:7f); the query after a loss answered in ~10 ms in most cases. Direction (request or reply lost) cannot be told from read-only queries.
- Bursts: one outage of three consecutive losses (>= 9 s without reply, t = 76-85 s); otherwise isolated losses.
- Slow replies: routine spikes 80-136 ms about twice a second (back-to-back phase: >100 ms 7/2000, max 136 ms); one 5 s episode where every reply took 250-420 ms (10 of 3215 > 250 ms, none 420-1000 ms).
- Consequence: the pulse end (after an idle of the pulse length) and the first poll query are the most exposed transactions, which explains why 1000/2000 ms pulses failed the 400 ms limit.

4. Simulator
- Already has: --udp-port, --drop-nth-reply n and --drop-first-replies n (command executed, reply withheld), fault file "<prefix> <reply> <count>" with reply "silent" (= request lost: logged in .events but not executed), monotonic timestamps in the .events log (allows ON/OFF edge timing).
- Missing: reply lost for a named command (executed), late reply. Prototyped (scratch, prototype_simulator.diff): fault reply "lost" executes and withholds the reply; "late:<ms>" executes and sends the reply <ms> later from a detached thread. Proposed additionally: a deterministic idle-loss option (lose the first datagram after >= N ms idle, every k-th time) to model the measured power-save behaviour.
- Prototype test (prototype_test.diff), RA 300/1100 ms pulse over UDP, physical length = .events time from :I1<guide period> to the executed :I1<tracking period>; asserts physical error < 300 ms and completion error < 400 ms:
  current driver: start reply lost physical +1055 ms / completion +1102 ms FAIL; end request lost +1063 / +1196 FAIL; poll :j2 reply lost during a 1100 ms pulse +972 / +1039 FAIL (reproduced twice).
  prototype fix (T 0.25 s): +256 / +335 PASS; +256 / +334 PASS; +4 / +64 PASS. Existing UDP cases (explicit URL, lost replies 1/7, autodetection) and all 15 guider cases (filter "guide") pass with the prototype.

5. Proposal
- UDP only: per-attempt reply timeout SYNSCAN_UDP_REPLY_TIMEOUT = 0.2 s (recommended; 0.25 s acceptable), 3 attempts kept (worst transaction ~0.6 s instead of 3 s). Serial unchanged (1 attempt, 1 s / 0.1 s), USB/serial EQ6-R/HEQ5 are not affected.
- Wait loop: keep waiting until the attempt deadline and ignore a datagram whose payload length does not match the command (0 for settings, 3 for :f, 2 for :g, 6 for other queries); a same-shape late reply to a retry of the same command is accepted (it is that command's answer).
- Drain on UDP with indigo_uni_wait_for_data(handle, 0) + full-size indigo_uni_read() instead of indigo_uni_discard(): drops stale datagrams whole, removes the 10 ms per command and the Windows WSAEMSGSIZE latch.
- synscan_now() -> indigo_monotonic_time() (also used for motion_deadline; check the autohome clock-offset tests).
- Poll guard: mount on_timer does not poll when a guide deadline is less than 0.2 s away (or passed) and reschedules itself 50 ms after it.
- Optional, not recommended now: verify-before-resend for :J (query :f, resend only when not running); removing the :f1 before the period change at the pulse edges (changes the recorded command manner); pre-wake/keep-alive query before the pulse end against the idle loss (measure after the basic fix first).
- Expected physical pulse error (RA, T = 0.2 s, ~10 ms RTT): no loss ~+10-20 ms (today up to +100 ms when a poll overlaps); one lost datagram at the risky points <= ~+0.22 s (today ~+1.03 s); two consecutive <= ~+0.43 s (today ~+2.05 s); three -> command fails after ~0.65 s and RA tracking is restored with ALERT (today ~3 s). Completion is late by the same amounts; a loss at the start that does not lengthen the pulse delays completion by <= T.
- Connect: explicit synscan://host with no mount answering fails after ~0.6 s instead of ~3 s; broadcast autodetection is library-bound (8 x 5 x 1 s + 7 x 1 s = ~47 s without a mount) and unchanged.
- Risks: SynScan Wi-Fi dongle / other ESP-based adapters with a serial hop to the motor board are slower (RTT a few tens of ms, unmeasured here) but well inside 0.2 s; a link with sustained >0.2 s latency (as in the 5 s episode) causes resends, harmless for idempotent commands and handled by the shape check, with the :J caveats above. Serial behaviour unchanged.
- Tests (phase 2): simulator "lost"/"late:<ms>" faults and idle-loss option; cases start reply lost, end request lost, poll reply lost during a pulse (all three fail on the current driver), DEC end (:K2) request lost, late reply of another shape during a setting command is ignored, late same-shape reply after a retry, connect with first :e1 lost, three consecutive losses at the pulse end restore tracking with ALERT; existing UDP and guider cases. Then recorded simulator run and non-interactive hardware run on the AZ-GTi.
- Hardware test limit: synscan_guide_pulse_accuracy measures public completion, not the physical pulse. With T = 0.2 s one lost datagram costs <= ~0.22 s plus latency spikes up to ~0.14 s, so 400 ms remains a sound limit for "at most one loss per pulse"; two consecutive losses in one pulse (rare) would still fail it. Recommend keeping 400 ms.

- A UDP command ends on the first reply. Every other send of it may still be answered: after success on attempt k, k-1 strays; after a '!' reply also k-1; after failure, all k sends. They are recorded with the command's reply length and the deadline last send + SYNSCAN_UDP_STRAY_WINDOW (0.5 s, conservative: the consumed reply may be the late one of an earlier send).
- Window: on the AZ-GTi replies took up to 0.42 s (a 5 s episode of 0.25-0.42 s replies), one reply in 3215 arrived 1.58 s late; 0.5 s covers all but that outlier.
- Before every send (each attempt) the driver reads and drops the datagrams already there (zero wait, whole datagrams), each one counting down an outstanding stray of its length. A query (reply length > 0) whose length equals an outstanding stray's first waits, bounded by that deadline, until those strays have arrived or expired. A command with a different reply length does not wait: the length check rejects the stray (and counts it down) while it waits for its own reply. A setting ("=" reply) does not wait either: an "=" carries no value, and waiting would hold the end of an RA guide pulse after every repeated start (start reply lost: +0.4 s instead of +0.2 s).
- After that, a datagram of the command's length that arrives while it waits is its reply; any other length is skipped. Serial unchanged.
- What remains possible: a stray later than its 0.5 s window (seen once in 3215 queries, at 1.58 s) that arrives while a query of the same length waits is taken as its reply, one wrong reading published once (the next poll corrects it); one arriving between commands is dropped by the next drain. A stray "=" can be taken as the acknowledgement of a later setting; it hides a lost request of that setting only if that request is lost too (both rare). Late '!' replies are not tracked (out of scope).
- Cost: only after a repeated command, and only for the next query of the same length (at most until 0.5 s after the last send). Under sustained 300 ms replies every query takes two sends and the next same-length query waits for the second reply; polls stay correct and slower.

Final rule (indigo_mount_synscan.driver: synscan_add_stray, synscan_take_stray, synscan_expire_strays, synscan_foreign_stray_deadline, synscan_drain_udp, synscan_command, synscan_read_response):
- Every UDP send is recorded when it is written: the full command text, the payload length of its reply and a deadline of send time + 0.5 s (SYNSCAN_UDP_STRAY_WINDOW; AZ-GTi late replies up to 0.42 s, one outlier 1.58 s in 3215). Up to 16 outstanding sends, the oldest is forgotten when full.
- A reply the command accepts (or a '!' reply) is accounted to the oldest outstanding send of that same command. Taking the oldest leaves the later deadlines, which cover the send whose reply is really still on its way. Sends that got no reply stay outstanding as strays until their own deadline.
- "Same command" is the full command text including axis and argument (":f1" and ":f2", ":j1" and ":j2", ":q1010000" and ":q2010000" differ). For queries only the axis and, for :q, the inquiry code are arguments, and they select different values, so they must be different commands. Settings carry their argument (":I1<period>"); since settings never wait, their identity only decides which send a datagram is accounted to.
- Before a send, the datagrams already there are read and dropped without waiting, each accounted to an outstanding send of this command with that length first, otherwise to the oldest send of any command with that length (other lengths: the oldest send of that length). A query first waits, bounded by their deadlines, until no send of ANOTHER command with the same reply length is outstanding. Outstanding sends of the same command never make it wait: a late answer to the same query is a valid answer to it. Commands with another reply length and settings do not wait.
- While a command waits for its own reply, a datagram of its length is its answer; any other length is accounted to the oldest send of that length and skipped. If the answer taken is a late one to an earlier send of the same command, the reply to the new send stays outstanding as that command's stray, so the count does not drift.
- Within one command's retries the drain before attempt 2 accounts a late attempt-1 reply to attempt 1's own record (the reviewer's accounting nuance), not to another command's stray.
- Residual: a reply later than its send + 0.5 s that lands while a query of the same length to another command waits is taken once as that query's reading; a late "=" may acknowledge a later setting; late '!' replies are not tracked. Serial unchanged; no library or generator change.

The marker is sent only after the command's reply was read, never pipelined (the controller drops pipelined requests).
